title: Scaling to Long Horizons — Ross Taylor & Chengxi Taylor, General Reasoning

primary.label: Post-Training & Continual Learning
primary.rationale: The talk's central subject is reinforcement learning for language models—PPO with verifiable rewards, value models, RLHF, reward models, and the training mechanics of long-horizon RL including gradient variance, credit assignment, bootstrapping, and off-policy staleness. Ross describes a concrete post-training recipe (continued pre-training on Llama 2 followed by PPO with a value model initialized from an outcome reward model), and Chengxi's entire segment focuses on RL training challenges and trade-offs (value models vs GRPO, pipeline RL, bootstrapping bias). The talk is fundamentally about adapting models after pretraining through RL methods.

secondary.label: Evaluation, Testing & Benchmarking
secondary.rationale: A significant portion of the talk presents the Kelly benchmark, where frontier models were evaluated on a real-world football trading task with $100K stakes over a one-year horizon. All models lost money, revealing fundamental limitations. The talk also implicitly evaluates Galactica against PaLM, Chinchilla, and GPT-3.5 on math and reasoning benchmarks.

secondary.label: Context Engineering & Memory
secondary.rationale: The talk discusses compaction (generate, summarize, continue) as essential for long-horizon tasks, context tools including file system tools (scratchpads for reasoning), self-search tools (searching previous trajectories), and archive tools (building on prior results). The inadequacy of current context windows (1M tokens) versus task requirements (tens of billions of tokens for Fermat's Last Theorem) is a key theme.

secondary.label: Agent Architecture & Harnesses
secondary.rationale: Long-horizon RL is framed around making agents coherent over extended periods. The talk discusses agent tool usage patterns (file system, self-search, archive tools) and the infrastructure needed to support long-running agent trajectories. However, the focus is more on the RL training mechanics than on agent loop or planner design per se.

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The RL methods, value models, bootstrapping, pipeline RL, and the openreward.ai platform with 350+ environments are all cross-domain, applicable across many task types rather than a single vertical.

domains.label: Finance & Trading
domains.rationale: The Kelly benchmark is explicitly a financial trading task—frontier models were given $100K to trade Premier League football matches. This real-world trading evaluation is a major demonstration in the talk.

domains.label: Scientific Research
domains.rationale: Galactica was a scientific language model; the talk covers scientific reasoning, math benchmarks, and the connection between curated scientific data and model capabilities. Fermat's Last Theorem is used as an illustrative long-horizon intellectual task.

summary: This talk by Ross Taylor (CEO of General Reasoning) and Chengxi Taylor covers two major themes: (1) a historical case study of Galactica and the critical role of RL in LLM products, and (2) the frontiers of long-horizon reinforcement learning. Ross recounts his journey from Papers With Code (acquired by Meta in 2019) through leading Galactica at Meta AI—a scientifically strong base model released two weeks before ChatGPT that failed commercially because it lacked RLHF. Galactica pioneered data efficiency (105B tokens vs trillions), multi-epoch training (the four-epoch rule), and thinking tokens as internal working memory, outperforming PaLM 540B and GPT-3 on scientific benchmarks with far less compute. Ross then describes an unpublished RL recipe (RSP): continued pre-training of Llama 2 on math/science data, then PPO with verifiable rewards using a value model initialized from a strong outcome reward model. This achieved SOTA on math but lacked inference-time scaling behaviors like backtracking and reflective reasoning. The lesson was the bitter lesson: better base models, more RL compute, and bigger context windows were the missing ingredients. Chengxi then reframes long horizon as a mindset requiring patience, identifying three core challenges: gradient variance scaling with trajectory length, sparse rewards, and credit assignment. Value models (critics) reduce variance and enable bootstrapping—getting reward signal before episode end like dopamine—but are more complex than GRPO and introduce value model bias. Context tools include file system scratchpads, self-search over previous trajectories, and archive tools for building on prior results. GR's KellyBench benchmark gave frontier models $100K to trade Premier League football matches over a one-year horizon; all lost money, featured in the Financial Times. This reveals the AI industry's bias toward coding/procedural tasks and the need for better environments and real-world simulation. GR's OpenReward platform hosts 350+ RL environments via a single API endpoint. On compute, pipeline RL trades off-policy staleness (acceptable up to ~8 steps) against GPU utilization, but week-long inferences exceed this constraint.
whyItMatters: This talk weaves together a historical narrative and a forward-looking research agenda connected by a single thread: reinforcement learning is the critical ingredient that transforms a capable base model into a useful reasoning system, but current RL methods break down at long horizons. The Galactica story establishes that RLHF was the differentiator between commercial success and failure, while the unpublished RSP recipe shows that even sophisticated RL (PPO with verifiable rewards and value models) cannot substitute for the bitter lesson of scale. The long-horizon segment then identifies exactly where current RL methods fail: gradient variance, sparse rewards, credit assignment, and the infrastructure constraint of pipeline RL. Value models, bootstrapping, compaction, and context tools are presented as algorithmic and engineering responses to these challenges, while KellyBench provides the empirical evidence that these responses are not yet sufficient. The OpenReward platform represents the infrastructure layer needed to build better environments. Together, these concepts trace the arc from 'RL is necessary' through 'RL at long horizons is hard' to 'here is what we are building to solve it,' making the talk both a cautionary historical case study and a research roadmap.
temporalContext: The video was published on July 31, 2026. The talk references events spanning 2019 (Papers With Code acquisition by Meta) through 2022 (Galactica and ChatGPT releases) to 2026 (OpenReward launch in March, KellyBench release in April). At the time of the talk, OpenReward hosted 350+ environments (since grown to 370+ by August 2026). The KellyBench results were approximately 3 months old at the time of recording. The talk was delivered during a period of rapid development in reasoning models, post-DeepSeek O1, with the field actively exploring long-horizon RL as the next frontier. Research was conducted as of August 23, 2026.

concepts.name: RLHF as the critical differentiator for LLM products
concepts.explanation: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback was the key pipeline that made ChatGPT a commercial product while Galactica—released two weeks earlier with a comparable base model—failed. InstructGPT had already demonstrated that a 1B parameter model with RLHF could outperform 175B parameter models without it. This establishes that post-training RL, not just base model quality, determines product viability.
concepts.importance: This is the central thesis of the first half of the talk and a foundational lesson for AI engineering: base model quality is necessary but insufficient; the post-training RL pipeline is what creates a usable product.

concepts.name: PPO with verifiable rewards and value models
concepts.explanation: The unpublished RSP recipe involved continued pre-training of Llama 2 on math/science data, then PPO with verifiable rewards using a value model initialized from a strong outcome reward model. This achieved SOTA on math reasoning but could not produce inference-time scaling behaviors (backtracking, reflective reasoning) without better base models and more compute.
concepts.importance: This represents a concrete, production-tested RL recipe for reasoning tasks, and its limitations directly motivate the bitter lesson: algorithmic sophistication alone cannot substitute for scale.

concepts.name: Thinking tokens as internal working memory
concepts.explanation: Galactica introduced thinking tokens—internal working memory within special tags that allowed the model to perform inference-time computation before producing an answer. This predates the mainstream adoption of chain-of-thought reasoning and represents an early architectural approach to structured reasoning.
concepts.importance: Thinking tokens are a foundational concept in the evolution toward reasoning-capable LLMs. Understanding their origin in Galactica provides historical context for modern chain-of-thought and reasoning token approaches.

concepts.name: Data efficiency and multi-epoch training
concepts.explanation: Galactica was trained on only 105 billion tokens (vs trillions in Chinchilla) by curating high-quality scientific text and using multi-epoch training (the four-epoch rule of thumb). This achieved superior performance with an order of magnitude less compute, demonstrating that data quality and training strategy can substitute for raw data volume.
concepts.importance: This challenges the prevailing assumption that more data is always better, showing that curated, high-quality data with multi-epoch training can achieve frontier performance with dramatically less compute.

concepts.name: Long horizon RL challenges: gradient variance, sparse rewards, credit assignment
concepts.explanation: Three core challenges make long-horizon RL fundamentally harder: (1) gradient variance scales with trajectory length, making training unstable; (2) rewards are sparse, providing little learning signal; (3) credit assignment—determining which actions contributed to the outcome—becomes intractable over long sequences.
concepts.importance: These challenges define the research frontier for long-horizon RL and motivate the specific algorithmic and infrastructure choices discussed in the talk, including value models, bootstrapping, and pipeline RL.

concepts.name: Value models (critics) for variance reduction and bootstrapping
concepts.explanation: Value models reduce gradient variance by providing expected value estimates, fit naturally with compaction, encourage batch diversity, and enable bootstrapping—generating reward signal before the episode ends, analogous to dopamine in biological systems. However, they are more complex than GRPO, require training a separate model, and introduce value model bias when used for bootstrapping.
concepts.importance: Value models are the primary algorithmic tool proposed for addressing long-horizon RL challenges. Understanding their benefits and trade-offs is essential for anyone building RL systems for extended tasks.

concepts.name: The bitter lesson in reasoning
concepts.explanation: Ross frames the failure of the RSP recipe to produce inference-time scaling as a manifestation of the bitter lesson: better base models, more RL compute, and bigger context windows—not algorithmic sophistication—were what ultimately enabled emergent reasoning behaviors like those in DeepSeek O1.
concepts.importance: The bitter lesson is one of the most important principles in AI engineering. This talk provides a concrete, personal case study of learning it through experience, making it more tangible than abstract formulations.

concepts.name: KellyBench: long-horizon sequential decision-making benchmark
concepts.explanation: GR constructed the KellyBench benchmark where frontier models were given $100K to build ML models for trading Premier League football matches over a one-year horizon. All frontier models lost money (mean ROI from -89.6% to -7.9%), featured on the front page of the Financial Times. This demonstrates AI's fundamental weakness at open-ended, real-world, long-horizon tasks.
concepts.importance: KellyBench provides concrete, quantified evidence that current frontier models fail at long-horizon real-world tasks, grounding the theoretical challenges in measurable outcomes and attracting public attention to AI limitations.

concepts.name: Industry bias toward coding and procedural tasks
concepts.explanation: Chengxi argues the AI industry is too biased toward coding and procedural tasks with limited solution spaces, leading to insufficient focus on open-ended tasks that capture real-world complexity and uncertainty. This bias results in models that excel at bounded problems but fail at genuinely open-ended, multi-agent scenarios.
concepts.importance: This critique has direct implications for how AI engineering teams should prioritize environment design, evaluation, and training task selection. It challenges the field to move beyond coding benchmarks toward richer, more realistic task domains.

concepts.name: Pipeline RL infrastructure
concepts.explanation: The systems engineering challenge of orchestrating reinforcement learning training where rollouts are generated asynchronously and consumed by the training loop. The core trade-off is off-policy staleness (how many steps old the rollout data is) versus GPU utilization (keeping GPUs busy). Up to ~8 steps of staleness is acceptable, but long-horizon inferences spanning weeks exceed this limit, forcing either GPU idleness or bootstrapping with value models.
concepts.importance: This is a critical infrastructure design problem for any team building RL training systems for long-horizon tasks. It determines whether RL training is even feasible for tasks whose episodes span days or weeks.

concepts.name: RL environment standardization via API
concepts.explanation: General Reasoning's OpenReward platform hosts 350+ RL environments accessible through a single API endpoint, built on the Open Reward Standard specification. This standardizes how language models connect to RL environments for training and evaluation, abstracting away environment-specific integration complexity.
concepts.importance: Standardizing environment interfaces is a foundational engineering problem for the RL ecosystem, analogous to standardizing model APIs for inference. It enables reproducibility, interoperability, and faster experimentation cycles.

concepts.name: Context tools for long-horizon agents
concepts.explanation: Three categories of tools designed to help agents maintain coherence over long horizons: (1) file system tools (scratchpad for persistent intermediate reasoning), (2) self-search tools (searching previous trajectories for relevant information), and (3) archive tools (building on prior results, though cheating must be guarded against). These are engineering solutions to the inadequacy of context windows for truly long tasks.
concepts.importance: Tool design for agents is a core software engineering challenge in the agent architecture space. These tools represent a practical design pattern for extending agent coherence beyond context window limits.

concepts.name: Compaction as a systems pattern
concepts.explanation: Compaction is the pattern of generate, summarize, continue—allowing an agent to compress its working context periodically rather than retaining the full trajectory. RL is applied to both the compaction step and the task itself. This is a software engineering approach to managing information loss over long sequences.
concepts.importance: Compaction is a key engineering pattern for any system that must operate over time scales exceeding its working memory. It bridges the gap between finite context windows and potentially unbounded task durations.

sections.title: Introduction and Background
sections.summary: Ross Taylor introduces himself as CEO of GR, a London-based RL company, formerly reasoning lead at Meta AI working on Llama and Galactica. He outlines the two-part talk structure: his personal perspective on the golden age of language modeling (2020-2023) and Chengxi on next frontiers.

sections.title: Papers With Code and Meta Acquisition
sections.summary: Ross describes Papers With Code as a London startup acquired by Meta in 2019, leading to Galactica and post-training for Llama 2 and 3. He credits this small team with originating the open-weight revolution.

sections.title: The Galactica Story
sections.summary: Galactica launched two weeks before ChatGPT. Both had good base models, but ChatGPT had RLHF while Galactica shipped as a raw base model demo. Ross frames this as a natural experiment showing RL provides value. InstructGPT had already shown a 1B model with RLHF outperforming 175B models. The Galactica demo triggered public alarm over hallucinated content.

sections.title: Galactica's Strengths: Curated Data and Thinking Tokens
sections.summary: Galactica outperformed PaLM, Chinchilla, and GPT-3.5 with less compute, pioneering data efficiency (105B tokens), multi-epoch training (the four-epoch rule), and thinking tokens—internal working memory within tags for inference-time computation before answers.

sections.title: Unpublished RL Recipe and the Bitter Lesson
sections.summary: Ross describes RSP: continued pre-training of Llama 2 on math/science, then PPO with verifiable rewards and a value model initialized from an outcome reward model. This achieved SOTA on math but lacked inference-time scaling behaviors. The lesson: better base models, more RL compute, and bigger context windows—pure bitter lesson—were what DeepSeek O1 needed to emerge.

sections.title: Transition to Long Horizon Frontiers
sections.summary: Ross reflects on being defeated by ChatGPT and O1 but not deterred, founding GR to tackle big tasks. He hands over to Chengxi to discuss next frontiers.

sections.title: Long Horizon as a Mindset
sections.summary: Chengxi reframes long horizon as a mindset requiring patience, not just engineering. He uses Fermat's Last Theorem (10+ years of work, tens of billions of tokens) versus current 1 million token context windows to illustrate the gap. Compaction—generate, summarize, continue—is proposed, with RL applied to both compaction and the task.

sections.title: Three Challenges of Long Horizon RL
sections.summary: Chengxi identifies three core issues: gradient variance scales with length, sparse rewards, and credit assignment. This section ends mid-discussion, to be continued.

sections.title: Value Models, Tools, and Bootstrapping
sections.summary: Chengxi explains value models (critics) reduce variance, fit compaction, encourage batch diversity, and enable bootstrapping—getting signal before episode end like dopamine—but are more complex than GRPO and require training a separate model. Context tools include file system tools (scratchpad), self-search tools (searching previous trajectories), and archive tools (building on prior results, with cheating risk).

sections.title: Kelly Benchmark: Football Trading
sections.summary: GR constructed the Kelly benchmark, featured on the front page of the Financial Times, where frontier models were given $100K to build ML models trading Premier League football matches over a one-year horizon. All models lost money, capturing public imagination about AI's limitations.

sections.title: Why Models Struggle at Long Horizon
sections.summary: Chengxi attributes model weakness to industry bias toward coding and procedural tasks with limited solution spaces, insufficient focus on open-ended tasks capturing real-world complexity and uncertainty, and inadequate simulation of multi-agent real-world environments with other players.

sections.title: Off-Policy Staleness vs GPU Utilization
sections.summary: Pipeline RL trades off-policy staleness against GPU utilization. Off-policy up to ~8 steps is acceptable, but long-horizon inferences spanning weeks exceed this constraint, forcing GPU idleness or bootstrapping with value models, which introduces value model bias. Infrastructure matters; GR's openreward.ai platform hosts 350+ environments via a single API endpoint, used internally and by frontier and new labs.

sections.title: Conclusion: Long Horizon as a Mindset
sections.summary: Chengxi summarizes: the long horizon journey requires new thinking on algorithms, environments, and compute. Despite challenges and trade-offs, long horizon is a mindset essential for solving humanity's biggest problems, and is the mission of General Reasoning, a London-based AI research company.

organization.name: General Reasoning
organization.summary: General Reasoning (GR) is a London-based AI research company founded in 2025, focused on training models that can work, communicate, and coordinate over long horizons. Research domains include reinforcement learning, multi-agent systems, and environment design. Founded by ex-Meta AI researchers including Ross Taylor (Co-Founder & CEO) and Chengxi Taylor (Co-Founder & President), the team previously drove open language models at Meta including Galactica, Llama 2, and Llama 3, and contributed research innovations including thinking tokens, data-scarce training methods, and early RL methods for LLMs. GR builds OpenReward (openreward.ai), a platform hosting 370+ RL environments via a single API endpoint, and KellyBench, a long-horizon evaluation benchmark where all frontier models lost money trading Premier League football matches. Backed by creators of PyTorch and TensorFlow. Raised $10.9M seed funding in July 2025. UK legal entity General Reasoning Ltd (Company No. 16515063, incorporated June 12, 2025), US legal entity General Reasoning, Inc. registered in San Francisco. Headquartered in Shoreditch, London with approximately 8-10 employees.

technologies.label: PPO with verifiable rewards and value models (RSP recipe)
technologies.primary: PPO with verifiable rewards and value models
technologies.summary: The RSP recipe represents a concrete, production-tested RL training technique for reasoning tasks: continued pre-training of Llama 2 on math/science data, followed by PPO with verifiable rewards using a value model initialized from a strong outcome reward model. This achieved SOTA on math reasoning but could not produce inference-time scaling behaviors (backtracking, reflective reasoning) without better base models and more compute. The talk frames this as a personal encounter with the bitter lesson: algorithmic sophistication alone cannot substitute for scale of base models, RL compute, and context windows. Value models serve as the key differentiator from simpler approaches like GRPO, enabling variance reduction, compaction compatibility, batch diversity, and bootstrapping, at the cost of additional complexity and value model bias.
technologies.role: This is the primary technique discussed in the first half of the talk. Ross Taylor presents the RSP recipe as a personal case study that taught him the bitter lesson about scale versus algorithmic sophistication in RL for reasoning.

technologies.label: Galactica model family
technologies.summary: Galactica is a scientific language model family developed by Ross Taylor's Papers With Code team at Meta AI, ranging from 125M to 120B parameters. It pioneered three key innovations: data-efficient pre-training (105B tokens of curated scientific text versus trillions in competitors), multi-epoch training (the four-epoch rule of thumb), and thinking tokens—internal working memory within special tags for inference-time computation that predates mainstream chain-of-thought. Galactica outperformed GPT-3 (68.2% vs 49.0% on LaTeX), Chinchilla (41.3% vs 35.7% on math MMLU), and PaLM 540B (20.4% vs 8.8% on MATH) with an order of magnitude fewer parameters. Released November 16, 2022—two weeks before ChatGPT—it served as a natural experiment: a strong base model without RLHF failed commercially while ChatGPT with RLHF succeeded.
technologies.role: Galactica is the central case study in the first half of the talk, used to illustrate that a strong base model is insufficient without RL, and to highlight pioneering contributions (thinking tokens, data efficiency) that later became mainstream.

technologies.label: OpenReward platform
technologies.summary: OpenReward is General Reasoning's open platform for serving RL environments at scale through a single API endpoint, built on the Open Reward Standard specification. Launched March 24, 2026 with 330+ environments, it has grown to 370+ as of August 2026. The platform standardizes how language models connect to RL environments for training and evaluation, abstracting away environment-specific integration complexity. This is analogous to standardizing model APIs for inference but for the environment side of RL training. The platform is used internally by GR and by frontier and new labs, and serves as the infrastructure layer for the pipeline RL approach discussed in the talk, where off-policy staleness (acceptable up to ~8 steps) is traded against GPU utilization.
technologies.role: OpenReward is presented as GR's infrastructure contribution to the RL ecosystem, hosting 350+ environments via a single API endpoint. It is discussed in the context of pipeline RL and the compute challenges of long-horizon training.

technologies.label: KellyBench long-horizon benchmark
technologies.summary: KellyBench is General Reasoning's benchmark for long-horizon sequential decision making, where frontier models are given $100K starting capital to build ML models for trading Premier League football matches over a full 2023-24 season. All frontier models lost money (mean ROI from -89.6% to -7.9%), requiring 500-1000 tool calls and 100K-1.7M tokens per episode. The benchmark was featured on the front page of the Financial Times (April 10, 2026) and is available as an open-access API endpoint on OpenReward. KellyBench demonstrates that current models fail at open-ended, real-world, long-horizon tasks, revealing the AI industry's bias toward coding and procedural tasks with limited solution spaces. The talk argues that better environments and real-world simulation—including multi-agent complexity with other players having different goals—are needed, not just bigger context windows.
technologies.role: KellyBench is the key empirical demonstration in the second half of the talk, providing concrete evidence that frontier models fail at long-horizon real-world tasks and motivating GR's research agenda on long-horizon RL.

Transcript's claim of 350+ is consistent with platform growth from 330+ at launch to 370+ currently.

resources.title: OpenReward
resources.why: Live OpenReward platform showing 370+ RL environments as of search date (August 2026), consistent with the transcript's claim of 350+ at the time of the talk (July 2026). Built on the Open Reward Standard for serving RL environments to train and evaluate language model agents.

resources.title: General Reasoning GitHub Organization
resources.why: Official GitHub organization for General Reasoning with 12 public repositories including firehorse (OpenReward environment harnesses), ether (scientific reasoning environment), and LAB-Bench evals. Created February 6, 2025.

resources.title: Introducing KellyBench
resources.why: Official KellyBench announcement, confirming all frontier models lost money trading 2023-24 Premier League football matches with 100K starting bankroll (paper uses GBP). Best model GPT-5.4 at -8% average ROI (original), Claude Opus 4.7 at -3.7% (updated). Featured in Financial Times and The Times on April 10, 2026. Includes full leaderboard, sophistication rubric, and compute statistics.

resources.title: Research | General Reasoning
resources.why: GR's research focus on long-horizon capabilities, RL, environment design. KellyBench research published April 2026.

resources.title: What is OpenReward?
resources.why: Official documentation for OpenReward, describing the platform for hosting RL environments to train and evaluate language model agents, built on the Open Reward Standard specification for connecting language models to RL environments.

resources.title: Galactica: A Large Language Model for Science
resources.why: Primary research paper for Galactica, led by Ross Taylor. Confirms training on 106 billion tokens of scientific text (transcript says 105B, minor rounding), model sizes from 125M to 120B, benchmark results (68.2% vs 49.0% vs GPT-3 on LaTeX, 41.3% vs 35.7% vs Chinchilla on math MMLU, 20.4% vs 8.8% vs PaLM 540B on MATH). Note: paper compares to GPT-3, not GPT-3.5 as stated in transcript. Published November 16, 2022, two weeks before ChatGPT (November 30, 2022).

resources.title: facebook/galactica-120b
resources.why: Official HuggingFace model page for Galactica 120B, confirming the model was open-sourced by Meta AI, trained on 106 billion tokens of scientific text, and developed by the Papers With Code team at Meta AI. Model sizes range from 125M (mini) to 120B (huge).

resources.title: Ross Taylor - Personal Website
resources.why: Ross Taylor is co-founder and CEO of General Reasoning. Previously led reasoning team at Meta AI on Llama 3 and Llama 2. Research lead on Galactica in 2022. Co-founded Papers With Code, acquired by Meta in 2019.

resources.title: Facebook quietly acquired another UK AI startup and almost no one noticed
resources.why: Facebook acquired Atlas ML (Deeptide Ltd) in December 2019 for approximately $40 million. Atlas ML was behind Papers With Code, co-founded by Robert Stojnic and Ross Taylor.

resources.title: KellyBench: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Sequential Decision Making
resources.why: Primary research paper for KellyBench, authored by GR team including Chengxi Taylor and Ross Taylor. Confirms all frontier models lost money on average over five seeds on 2023-24 Premier League season, with mean ROI ranging from -89.6% to -7.9%. Models used 500-1000 tool calls and 100K-1.7M tokens per episode. Published April 30, 2026.

resources.title: paperswithcode/galai
resources.why: Official GitHub repository for Galactica, showing model sizes from 125M (mini) to 120B (huge), confirming the Papers With Code team at Meta AI developed it. Links to galactica.org for the paper and additional documentation.

resources.title: GeneralReasoning/KellyBench
resources.why: Live KellyBench environment on OpenReward, confirming the benchmark is available as an open-access API endpoint for long-horizon sequential decision-making in sports betting markets. Requires 500-900 tool calls per episode over a full Premier League season.

resources.title: AI punters lose their shirts on Premier League bets
resources.why: Financial Times article covering KellyBench results, published April 10, 2026. Transcript claim of front-page placement could not be independently verified.

resources.title: Ross Taylor - LinkedIn
resources.why: Ross Taylor is Co-Founder & CEO at General Reasoning (Feb 2025-present). Previously Research Engineer at Facebook AI (Dec 2019-Apr 2024). Co-founded Atlas ML (Papers With Code), acquired by Meta in 2019.
